content.text: India Post GDS is one of the few forms that states its rules in
shapes
, not just sizes. The photo is
and the signature is
. If you crop a photo to a square or a signature to a long thin strip, it will not match, even when the KB is right.
The numbers from the Schedule-II 2026 notice
Photo:
JPG, recommended 320×400 px, 30–100 KB, 72–150 DPI, plain white or light background, face filling 70–80% of the image, no shadows or red-eye.
Signature:
JPG, recommended 300×120 px, 20–100 KB, 72–150 DPI, black or blue pen on white paper, signature filling 70–80% of the image, no borders or extra marks, no typed or digital signature.
SahiSize writes 150 DPI, the top of the allowed range.
Doing it on a phone
Sit facing a window. Hold the phone at eye level, about an arm’s length away.
In SahiSize, crop so your head and the top of your shoulders fill the 4:5 frame. The face should take most of the space; this is tighter than a typical selfie.
Sign on white paper with a dark pen. Sign slowly; the notice warns against shaky or pixelated signatures.
Crop close to the ink in the 5:2 frame so it covers 70–80% of the image. Clean signature removes paper edges and shadows, which count as “extra marks”.
Save both files and pick them from your Downloads folder in the form.
What you do not upload
GDS selection is based on the Class 10 marks you type into the form. There is no certificate upload at the application stage; documents are checked later.
Timing
India Post runs several schedules a year. In 2026, Schedule-II opened in late August. Forms have usually appeared around January and August.
If the portal still rejects it
A tight 320×400 crop can save under 30 KB; Auto-fit raises the quality to cross it. If the signature is refused, check for a visible paper edge or a shadow.
